title: Wednesday Plan (guest teacher)
note: Ms. Herrick is out sick. 30-minute shortened day. NO building. 8th and 7th work in TinkerCAD from self-guided handouts; 6th solves net force puzzles on paper. One turn-in per class: the exit ticket on Google Classroom.

4th Period.goal: By the end of class, my potentiometer changes my LED's brightness, and I can read its value in the serial monitor.
4th Period.exitTicket: What range of numbers did you see in the serial monitor, and what happened to the LED as the number went up? (link pasted at the end)
prep: Blooket: 8th_Wed_Nov18_Blooket_Button (needs a host link from Ms. Herrick)
Handout 8th_Wed_Nov18_Circuits3_Dial on Google Classroom; exit ticket posted

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Tuesday (8th_Wed_Nov18_Blooket_Button).
tips: If the Blooket can't be hosted, skip it and give the 5 minutes to the main task.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed question, then read the goal aloud.
tips: Likely most-missed: what the 10 kΩ resistor does (keeps pin 2 LOW when not pressed).

segments.title: Step by step: wire the dial, see the numbers
segments.do: Students duplicate Blink, move the LED to pin 9, wire the potentiometer (5V, GND, middle leg to A0), and type the code from the page.
tips: Pin 13 can't dim; that's why the LED moves to pin 9.
Most common bugs: middle leg not on A0, Serial with a small s, missing ;.

segments.title: You do: dim the LED with the dial
segments.do: Start Simulation, open Serial Monitor, drag the knob, note min and max, then Share and copy the link.
tips: Answer key: 0 to 1023; as the number goes up, the LED gets brighter.

segments.title: Exit Ticket
segments.do: Answer on Google Classroom with a frame, then paste the link.
tips: Answer key: about 0 to 1023; bigger number = brighter LED.

watchFor: Students without Monday's design: they can start a new circuit and build it fresh

6th Period.topic: Cam and Follower, Day 3: add the follower
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, my follower sits on top of my cam.
6th Period.exitTicket: Name the 3 parts of your machine and what each one does.
prep: Handout 7th_Wed_Nov18_Cam_Day3 on Google Classroom; exit ticket posted
TinkerCAD class link for sign-in trouble: https://www.tinkercad.com/joinclass/ZS3NSEL8W

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Tuesday (7th_Wed_Nov18_Blooket_CamModel).
tips: If the Blooket can't be hosted, skip it and give the 5 minutes to the main task.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed question, then read the goal aloud.
tips: Likely most-missed: why the axle is thinner than the hole (so the cam can spin).

segments.title: You do: add the follower with Align
segments.do: Box 6×40×10, Align with the cam on the two middle dots, then Shift + up arrow ×4 so it touches the cam's edge.
tips: If Align moves the cam away from its axle: Ctrl + Z, press L, click the cam once so it stays still, then the dots.
Students who missed Tuesday: build the cam first from Tuesday's handout.

segments.title: Check from above
segments.do: TOP on the view cube; follower touches the cam's edge.

segments.title: Exit Ticket
segments.do: Answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Answer key: the cam spins and pushes; the follower rides on it and moves up and down; the axle is what the cam spins on.

watchFor: Students who never finished Tuesday's cam

7th Period.topic: Tensegrity, Day 3: net force puzzles (no building)
7th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can add up the forces in a force diagram to predict if an object moves, and which way.
7th Period.exitTicket: In puzzle B, what is the net force, and which way does the cart move?

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the Blooket reviewing Tuesday (6th_Wed_Nov18_Blooket_ForceDiagrams).
tips: If the Blooket can't be hosted, skip it and give the 5 minutes to the main task.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Go over the most-missed question, then read the goal aloud.
tips: Likely most-missed: which way the lamp's tension arrow points (up, along the string).

segments.title: Read: adding up forces
segments.do: Read the key words and the worked example aloud: 150 N − 100 N = 50 N to the right.
tips: Same direction add, opposite directions subtract.

segments.title: You do: 4 net force puzzles
segments.do: A with a partner; B, C, D alone. Write the math, draw a green net arrow or write balanced, say which way it moves.
tips: Answer key A: 80 − 80 = 0 N, balanced, no movement.
D: 20 up − 20 down = 0 N, balanced, the lamp stays still.

segments.title: Exit Ticket
segments.do: Answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Answer key: 30 N, to the right (toward the 90 N side).

watchFor: Students adding opposite forces instead of subtracting

accommodations: Goal read after the Blooket, numbered steps, worked example first, sentence frames on every exit ticket.
Key words with pictures, partner talk on puzzle A before writing, two frames per exit ticket.
Lexend Deca handouts, steps read aloud on request, speech-to-text OK, spelling not graded.
Short chunks, visual timer, partner checks after each step (7th), break pass.
Extended time, dictated exit tickets, intentional partners. Floors: 8th wires the dial and sees numbers (dimming optional); 7th adds the follower (check optional); 6th does puzzles A, B, D.
frameworks: Day 3 toward Thursday's products (8th circuit links, 7th TinkerCAD cam). 6th's product is being reworked while no building is possible.
Partners check each other's screens or puzzle A together; students help neighbors.
Self-guided handouts with everything on the page, one turn-in, 'you are not behind' on a sub day.
Apply (build/solve) moving into Analyze (the dial's range, 3-force puzzles).
